description: The plot illustrates knowledge-probing accuracy (ACC) on BioMedLM after applying different editing methods (Base, FT, IKE, MEND, MEMIT, ROME) as a function of co-occurrence number. The x-axis is labeled “Co-occurrence Number” and uses a logarithmic scale, with labeled ticks at 0, 10¹, 10², and 10³; the plotted points lie at four increasing co-occurrence levels spanning from the low single digits to a few thousand. The y-axis is labeled “ACC (%)”, uses a linear scale, and spans roughly from 38% up to about 66%, with visible labeled ticks at 40, 45, 50, 55, 60, and 65. The Base series is a black solid line with circular markers, increasing from about 38.5% at the smallest co-occurrence to ~41.8% at the next point, then to ~44.0% at the third point, and remaining near ~44.0% at the largest co-occurrence. FT is a blue solid line with downward-triangle markers, rising from ~40.0% to ~43.3% to ~46.1% and then to ~47.7% at the largest co-occurrence. IKE is a red solid line with upward-triangle markers, moving from ~43.0% to ~44.9% to ~46.6% and then to ~49.4%. MEND is a brown solid line with diamond markers, increasing from ~44.5% to ~48.9% to ~54.0% and then to ~56.5%. MEMIT is a purple solid line with pentagon-like markers, starting near ~43.8%, rising to ~51.1%, then to ~52.9%, and ending near ~54.8%. ROME is a green solid line with square markers, increasing from ~51.0% to ~57.2% to ~62.4% and reaching ~66.1% at the largest co-occurrence.
